A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Top-W research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite repagination and reordered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original Top-W benchmark results, parameter-sensitivity experiments, decoding timings, and creative-writing evaluations. Some comparator scores are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds Top-W evaluations at lower temperatures across the four main benchmarks.

M1.justification: The Wasserstein–entropy–mass objective, geometric potential, prefix-based subset update, and alternating decoder are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the candidate-pool and refinement configurations are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, GPQA, AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, and the same three creative-writing prompts. The added decoding temperatures change configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Min-p, Top-p, and Top-H remain the comparators in the corresponding benchmark, creative-writing, and runtime comparisons. Citation replacements do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The main benchmark temperature grid expands from {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} to {0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0}. Models, metrics, stated sample sizes, judging procedures, and default Top-W settings remain unchanged. The tuning-set description is newly disclosed information rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–2 extend temperature-sensitivity evidence into the lower-temperature regime, showing additional conditions where baselines remain competitive. The lambda/beta sensitivity plots, higher-beta creative-writing analysis, and runtime analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: The versions retain three-run GSM8K aggregation, four-run GPQA and benchmark judging, and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting over five creative-writing repeats. Appendix J's paired-seed and repeated-sampling descriptions are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–2 add substantial lower-temperature results across all four benchmarks and three models. These reveal additional baseline wins: for example, at T=0.5 on Qwen GSM8K, Min-p scores 75.89 versus Top-W's 75.44. Original-temperature scores and Tables 3–8 are unchanged; this is added evidence rather than improved performance under retained settings.

T1.justification: Section 3 withdraws the advertised monotonicity assertion in lambda, retaining only beta monotonicity and Corollary 3.5. The formal theorem statements, equations, and appendix proofs themselves remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the geometry-aware decoding contribution, prefix/singleton characterization, accuracy and creativity claims, and improvement of up to 33.7%. Updated introductory win counts summarize expanded evidence without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 adds a qualification about shrinking advantages and baseline wins at low temperatures. However, it replaces v1's accurate LLaMA GPQA exception at T=1.0 with an incorrect claim of remaining top or tied: Table 2 still gives Top-W 30.80 versus Top-p 32.81. Other mechanism explanations and impact cautions are retained.

D1.justification: v1 describes the hyperparameter grid and refinement without identifying the tuning data. v2's Appendix L specifies 50 randomly held-out AlpacaEval development examples and subsequent fixed hyperparameters across experiments. The grid and selected defaults are unchanged, so this improves documentation without establishing that tuning was rerun.

R1.justification: Li et al. (2023), Contrastive Decoding, replaces two Su/Collier contrastive-search references in the introduction and related work. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works; the positioning against probability-only and entropy-based decoding remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief explanations around Lemma 3.1, revises results summaries, removes a conflicting appendix metric description, and swaps the tuning and judge appendices. Bibliographic and proceedings text is updated, while the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain temperature rows, and Figures 1–2 change from three horizontally aligned panels to two upper panels and one lower panel. Algorithm 1 and Figure 3 move without substantive display changes. Figure 2 incorrectly changes its vertical-axis label from judge score to Accuracy (%).

improvement.justification: The lower-temperature comparisons make the empirical assessment more informative by exposing competitive baseline conditions, while the disclosed tuning holdout improves reproducibility. These benefits outweigh localized reporting regressions: the incorrect GPQA T=1.0 generalization and mislabeled MT-Bench axis. The improvement is limited because the method, formal proofs, and previously reported results remain essentially unchanged.
